title: Influence of Secondary Component Hardness When Cold Spraying Mixed Metal Powders on Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: relatively spherical
preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: degreased with ethanol and grit-blasted with 24 grit alumina. pre-heated by operating a single pass, without powder injection, at the given conditions

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: relatively poor/irregular coating

Experiments.Notes: Pure Sn on Steel. Note powder hardness: 7 ± 1 HV 0.01. Noted that hardness of tin in the coating was measured as between 12 ± 1 HV 0.01 and 14 ± 1 HV 0.01

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: Sn is relatively spherical, Al particles are spherical with some satellite particles.

preSprayedProperties.Substrate_Surface_Preparation: degreased with ethanol and grit-blasted with 24 grit alumina. pre-heated by operating a single pass, without powder injection, at the given conditions

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: powders mixed for 1h in a metal can

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: Good deposition coating condition. very low retention rate of secondary component (<1%)

Experiments.Notes: Sn-10Al on Steel. Note powder hardness: 7 ± 1 HV 0.01 (Sn), and  24 ± 2 HV0.01 (Al). Noted that hardness of tin in the coating was measured as between 12 ± 1 HV 0.01 and 14 ± 1 HV 0.01, and due to the low retention rate of SC in the coating, could be interpreted as coating hardness.
